newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks strong in morning, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks strong in morning, more gains seen.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks began Monday's session with strong gains, and traders said investor optimism should push prices higher with the Hang Seng index seen heading towards resistance at 12,000 points in the near term.
"It seems like there is quite a lot of overseas buying interest and I think the locals are pretty bullish on the market as well," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities.
The Hang Seng index was up 65.38 points at 11,824.77.
Turnover was HK$1.17 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.
"I think the index will probably go even higher. The market will meet resistance at around 12,000 points," Ho said.
James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said investors had been picking up laggards which was buoying the market.
"The laggards over the last couple of weeks are being bought up again and as a result I think things could generally look quite steady at these levels," he said.

"The important thing is no one is really willing to sell Hong Kong. People still feel that on a longer term view, on an interest rate cycle view, on a China liquidity view that Hong Kong is still acceptable at these levels," said Osborn.
He said investors had been increasing their weightings and saw no "serious or viable" alternative to Hong Kong.
Wah Tak Fung shares made their stock market debut on Monday and after a higher start, soon fell below their issue price.
The shares were offered at HK$1.88 per share and opened at HK$1.92 before falling back to HK$1.81.
Wah Tak Fung is a property developer.
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.00 to HK$81.75. The company is due to release its final results on Wednesday.
Amid optimism about property sales in the territory, Cheung Kong gained HK$0.75 to HK$58.25 and Henderson Land was up HK$0.75 at HK$65.75.

Shares in S.A.S. Dragon fell HK$0.09 to HK$0.59. The electronic components and fashion distributor and retailer reported a loss of HK$15.98 million in the six months ended June 30 compared to profit of HK$15.68 million.
Trading in Dransfield Holdings shares was suspended at the company's request pending an announcement. The shares closed at HK$0.475 on Friday.
HSBC Holdings was up HK$0.50 at HK$144.00 and Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$0.50 to HK$81.25.
